criteria.A: Shadow-table staging: build and validate the full target state in dedicated staging tables isolated from live reads, then publish with a single fenced activation commit that switches the installed-snapshot pointer.
criteria.B: Co-located versioned rows: write staged variants next to installed rows in the same tables with snapshot-id tags, keep live reads pinned to the installed snapshot, and activate by repointing that snapshot pointer.
criteria.C: Namespace-copy activation: duplicate the dataset into a fresh model namespace, validate the copy, then atomically re-alias each model to the new namespace in one fenced commit and retire the old namespace.

staging_design.instructions: From a failure-safety and simplicity standpoint, which staging design should the state engine implement, given that failed preparation must not disturb installed data, activation must be a single fenced commit inside one authority, progress must be resumable in bounded chunks, and row-version behavior must distinguish converted rows from renamed ones?
